description: A single-panel bright-field TEM micrograph (unlabelled, one image) of deformed Fe–25% Al, taken close to the [0 0 1] zone axis with a 1 1 0 imaging vector, which is marked by a black arrow in the lower-left corner; a black scale bar at the bottom left reads "0.2µm". The field is dominated by long, straight, near-parallel dislocation lines running diagonally across the grain, i.e. dislocations in near-screw orientation that stay straight over distances of many hundreds of nanometres, with some segments bowed or cusped and a few local tangles (a dark knot near the image centre and a fan-like bundle in the upper middle). Letter annotations mark specific configurations: "d" labels several narrow dislocation dipoles (top-right corner, upper right, right-centre and centre-left areas) and "p" labels two loose dislocation pairs in the lower right. Taken with the caption and citing text, the panel demonstrates that in the DO3-ordered Fe–25% Al the loosely coupled superdislocation partials (p) coexist with edge-dipole segments (d), and that these dislocations remain straighter and closer to screw orientation than in Fe–20% Al.
measured_quantities: imaging vector g = 1 1 0 (annotated by arrow, indices not printed in image)

observations.observation: A black scale bar printed at the bottom left of the micrograph is labelled '0.2µm'.
A black arrow in the lower-left corner of the image marks the diffraction vector g; the reflection indices themselves are not printed on the image.
The field is dominated by long, straight, roughly parallel dislocation lines running diagonally across the grain, giving a near-screw-dominated dislocation structure.
The letter 'd' is printed at several locations on the image (top-right corner, upper right, right-centre and centre-left), labelling narrow dislocation dipole segments.
The letter 'p' is printed at two locations in the lower-right region of the image, labelling loose dislocation pairs.
Localised dislocation tangles are visible, including a dark knot near the image centre and a fan-like bundle of closely spaced lines in the upper middle of the field.
The caption states the image is a bright field transmission electron micrograph showing dislocation pairs (p) and dipoles (d) in Fe–25% Al after deformation.
The caption states the zone axis is near [0 0 1] and that a 1 1 0 imaging vector (arrowed) is used for contrast; the zone axis is not annotated inside the image itself.
The citing text states that Fig. 9 shows a large number of near-screw dislocations in the deformed Fe–25% Al alloy, in which many loose pairs of dislocations can be distinguished.
The citing text states that +g and g imaging conditions were used to show that many of the pairs are loose superdislocation partials (marked p), while others are loose dipole pairs (marked d).
The citing text states that, compared with Fe–20% Al (Fig. 6), the dipole/pair segments in the Fe–25% Al alloy tend to remain more straight and close to the screw orientation.

The citing text associates the retention of loosely coupled dislocation pairs with the DO3 long-range order in Fe–25% Al, the APBI/APBII energies being too low to keep dislocations closely coupled as superdislocations.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph, 0.2 µm scale bar, black arrow in the lower-left marking the 1 1 0 imaging vector. Long straight near-screw dislocation lines run diagonally across the field; about five 'd' labels mark dislocation dipoles and two 'p' labels in the lower right mark loose dislocation pairs; local tangles and bowed segments occur near the centre and upper middle.

unreadable_items: No reflection indices, zone-axis label or diffraction pattern is printed inside the micrograph; the g vector is given only by an arrow and by the caption
Dislocation line directions and whether individual lines are exactly screw-oriented cannot be determined from this single image
The number of d/p labels cannot be counted with certainty because some annotation letters overlap dense dislocation tangles
